column1: Taken from the live AIMS intake (Syra risk profile, AIRA-DDA-2.0 proposal). Part A is the risk profile: 21 questions across 5 cards: 20 with a “?” button, plus the 'Type of AI use' picker on the first card. Only the 20 risk questions in Part A set the risk score; Type of AI use is a category only. Part B is the record and business-case questions, which are not part of risk scoring.

About the “Syra explains” column: in the app, clicking “?” asks Syra to explain the question live, so the wording varies from click to click. The text here is a standard plain-language explanation for each question. It can be fixed into the app as the default so every user sees the same wording.
PART A: RISK PROFILE QUESTIONS (used for risk scoring)

column1: Card: AI relationship  ·  Who builds it and where it runs  ·  2 questions + type picker

column4: How does this AI relate to JazzWorld?
column6: (No “?” button on this row.) AI For Us means using a tool another company makes, like Microsoft Copilot. AI By Us means JazzWorld builds or deploys it. AI Against Us means looking at how criminals could use AI against JazzWorld or its customers.
column7: None. Category only, per the AIRA scales document: By Us = a project we build, For Us = a licence or tool we acquire, Against Us = a threat report. It routes the review but does not change the risk score.

column4: Where will the AI run and process data?
column6: This asks where the computers that run the AI, and handle your data, are located. JazzWorld's own servers is the safest answer; a cloud service abroad like Azure or OpenAI is 'vendor abroad'; a free public tool, or not knowing, is the riskiest.
column7: Strategic / Sovereignty Dependency; escalation rule F5

column4: If needed, how easily could you switch to another model or vendor?
column6: If this vendor raised its prices, changed its terms or shut down, could we move to another AI provider without rebuilding everything? The harder it is to switch, the more we depend on them.
column7: Third-Party / Supplier Dependency

column1: Card: Data  ·  What information it uses  ·  4 questions

column4: What's the most sensitive information it will use?
column6: Think of the most private piece of information the AI will ever see, not the usual one. For example, if it mostly sees names but sometimes sees wallet balances, choose the financial option.
column7: Data Sensitivity, Personal Data Exposure, Privacy, Strategic / Sovereignty, Cybersecurity, Legal & Regulatory, Foreseeable Misuse; sets the Data weighting; rule F5

column4: Roughly how many people does it touch?
column6: How many people's data or experience does this AI touch? A tool for a few analysts is 'a handful'; a chatbot open to every Jazz customer is 'all subscribers'.
column7: Population Affected, Personal Data Exposure, Customer / Service Impact, Reputation, Societal Impact, Scale of Exposure; rules F5, F6

column4: Will that data leave JazzWorld, or could a vendor keep or train on it?
column6: Does the information go outside JazzWorld to a vendor? And could that vendor store it, or use it to improve its own AI? The vendor contract usually answers this.
column7: Privacy / Data Protection

column4: Will it combine records or work things out about people?
column6: Does the AI join different pieces of data about a person, or guess things about them, such as how likely they are to leave or repay a loan? Simply looking up one record is 'No'.
column7: Personal Data Exposure, Privacy, Fairness, Model / Data Susceptibility

column1: Card: Decisions  ·  What its output affects  ·  6 questions

column4: What role does the AI's output play?
column6: Who has the final say, the AI or a person? If staff read its suggestion and decide themselves, choose 'a person always decides'. If its result is applied without anyone deciding, choose 'decides automatically'.
column7: Decision Consequence, Human Oversight & Autonomy, Business Criticality, Financial Exposure, Customer / Employee / Individual Consequence; sets the Decision weighting; rules F2, F3, F7

column4: What could its output affect?
column6: What is the most serious thing the AI's output could change for someone? Saving staff time is low; changing someone's bill, eligibility or access to a loan or service is high.
column7: Decision Consequence, Human Rights, Fairness, Safety & Reliability, Transparency, Reputation, Societal Impact; rules F2, F3

column4: Who is affected by its outputs?
column6: Whose life or work changes because of what the AI produces? Staff who simply use it as a tool, employees being assessed by it, customers, or both.
column7: Decides which items apply: Customer Impact, Employee Impact, Individual Consequence, Customer / Service Impact, Reputation

column4: Could it affect vulnerable people, such as low-income, unbanked, elderly or low-literacy users, or minors?
column6: Could it affect people who are less able to protect themselves, like elderly, low-income, unbanked or low-literacy users, or children? If they are the main users, choose the last option.
column7: Vulnerable / Higher-Impact Groups, Human Rights, Fairness; rule F2

column4: Can affected people see why, and challenge the result?
column6: If the AI's result affects someone, can they find out why, and ask for it to be reviewed or changed? For example, a customer refused a service can ask a person to look again.
column7: Transparency & Explainability

column4: Does it touch regulated or legally sensitive activity?
column6: Does this touch an area with its own rules, like SBP rules for JazzCash banking or PTA rules for telecom? If it only handles personal data, 'general privacy rules' applies.
column7: Legal & Regulatory; rule F1

column1: Card: Actions  ·  What it can do  ·  5 questions

column4: What can the AI actually do?
column6: What is the most the AI can do by itself? Showing an answer is low; talking directly to customers is higher; changing records, accounts or payments is the highest.
column7: Business Criticality, Financial Exposure, Safety & Reliability, Human Oversight & Autonomy, Cybersecurity, Societal Impact; sets the Action weighting; rules F4, F7

column4: Who can start or use it?
column6: Who is able to start or use it? The more people who can use it, especially people outside JazzWorld or without logging in, the higher the chance it gets misused.
column7: Cybersecurity, Reputation, Scale of Exposure, Access Required, Skill Required, Foreseeable Misuse; rule F4

column4: How often will it run?
column6: How often is it used? A one-off analysis is 'rarely'; a customer chatbot answering all day is 'non-stop'.
column7: Frequency of Use, Duration / Persistence of Exposure, Resilience / Continuity

column4: If it breaks or gets things wrong, what happens?
column6: Imagine it stops working, or gives wrong answers, for a day. Could the team simply go back to doing it by hand, or would important services stop?
column7: Business Criticality, Customer / Service Impact, Operational Dependency, Financial Exposure, Resilience / Continuity

column4: What kind of AI is it?
column6: What kind of technology is it? Fixed rules follow set instructions; machine learning learns from data; generative AI (like ChatGPT) writes new content; an AI agent can use tools and take steps by itself.
column7: Safety & Reliability, Cybersecurity, Historical Occurrence, Change / Volatility, Technical Feasibility, Skill Required, Model / Data Susceptibility

column1: Card: Safeguards  ·  What keeps it safe  ·  3 questions

column4: Does a person approve before the AI's output takes effect?
column6: Before the AI's output reaches a customer or changes anything, does a trained person check and approve it? 'Only after the fact' means someone looks at it only once it has already gone out.
column7: Human Oversight Controls; rule F3

column4: Are guardrails and monitoring in place?
column6: Guardrails are protections such as blocking harmful answers, limiting what data the AI can see, and alerts when something goes wrong. Are these already built and tested, only planned, or missing?
column7: Preventive Controls, Detective Controls

column4: Is there a named owner, and evidence the safeguards were tested?
column6: Is one named person responsible for this AI, and is there proof, like test results, that its safeguards actually work? Without that evidence, every safeguard counts for less.
column7: Governance Controls, Control Validation / Testing; without evidence, all control scores are capped at Moderate (3)

column1: Total risk profile questions with a “?” button: 20

The old three Yes/No screening questions (sensitive data, affects decisions, interacts or acts) and their follow-ups are no longer asked. They are worked out from these answers for the ServiceNow record.
